title: Should Investors Buy Navitas Semiconductor Stock on the Dip?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions (manual English captions)
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Navitas Semiconductor is a buy on the dip. The story is exciting — high-voltage GaN/SiC power semiconductors for AI, defense and infrastructure, with signed contracts and a multi-year backlog driving Wall Street forecasts of +56% revenue growth in 2027 and +67% in 2028. But the financials are grim: revenue collapsed from >$90M TTM a couple of years ago to $36.5M TTM (-46%), 2025 revenue fell 45% YoY, cash flow from operations-to-sales is -182% and worsening, and ROIC is -64%. With negative earnings and cash flow, he uses forward price-to-sales: over 42x — expensive even for the expected growth. His DCF fair value is just over $3 versus ~$12 market. The stock whipsawed from ~$7 to over $30 and back below $10 in a matter of months. Call: NVTS HOLD with low conviction — 'right business, wrong price'; he's waiting on the sidelines for a cheaper entry or business improvement before it becomes attractive for long-term investors. First tracked call on NVTS; no flip.
